A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of 18 MLLMs, 17 misleader types, and six correction methods. All pages, including appendices, support comparison; relocated content can be distinguished from actual omissions.

before.justification: v3 reports original accuracy evaluations, paired-visualization consistency measurements, correction-method experiments, and supplementary analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original results of Experiments 1–3, including MLLM accuracy, Likert-scale consistency, and correction-method effectiveness.

M1.justification: Both versions propose the same six inference-time correction methods, including table-based QA and visualization redrawing with fallback to the original image. Shortened descriptions do not establish a changed procedure or component.

E1.justification: Coverage remains 143 misleading instances, 124 non-misleading instances, ChartQA's 2,500 instances, and four visualization pairs for Likert-scale evaluation. CALVI, CHARTOM, VLAT, real-world examples, and the 17 misleader types are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding main comparisons retain the same 18 MLLMs, random and published-human references, and six correction strategies evaluated using Qwen2VL-7B, Ovis1.6-9B, and InternVL2.5-8B. No comparator is replaced or added.

E3.justification: v4 omits the controlled MCQ-choice-order variation reported in v3 Section 3.1 and Table F4, narrowing the reported evaluation design. The primary dataset sizes, model configurations, and zero-shot setup remain unchanged; omitted implementation disclosures do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: The MCQ-choice-order sensitivity analysis in v3 Appendix F is removed. Analyses by misleader type, real-world versus synthetic data, redrawing failures, and paired table-extraction consistency remain; Figures C1 and E2 are relocated as Figures 5 and 8.

E5.justification: v4 substantially reduces statistical reporting: it removes Table F4's shuffled-order means, standard deviations, and three-seed information; Table D3's complete McNemar statistics and p-values; and Experiment 2's t statistics. Likert-scale standard deviations, paired-test p-values, and significance hatching remain. These are reporting losses, without evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: v4 removes Table F4's additional accuracy results, detailed statistical outcomes, and the statement that redrawing succeeds above 90% for other chart types. Retained results match, including 25.6% mean misleading-chart accuracy and table-based QA gains of 15.4–19.6 percentage points.

T1.justification: The misleader definitions and consistency criterion are retained. Neither version presents a theorem or proof framework, and no formal mathematical reasoning is added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction's second contribution drops v3's promise of maintaining accuracy on non-misleading visualizations, narrowing that statement to mitigating QA errors. The abstract retains the preservation wording while foregrounding both effective methods and the already reported 19.6-point maximum gain. The central vulnerability claim remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 omits v3 Section 3.4's explanation that five question-dependent misleader types cannot receive standardized warnings, losing an applicability qualification. The parametric-knowledge hypothesis, extraction bottleneck, accuracy trade-off, and three general limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: v4 omits the ±5% relaxed numeric-answer accuracy rule, top-p=1, warning-method exclusions, and explicit identification of ChartQA scores as previously reported. Core model, library, temperature, and inference-seed disclosures and the code/data link remain. These omissions reduce documentation without demonstrating implementation changes.

R1.justification: v4 replaces Jan et al.'s bioimage-analysis reference with Huang et al.'s chart-understanding survey and removes Doan's COVID-19 chart-misrepresentation reference. Positioning relative to visualization linters and parallel MLLM studies is largely retained; the Gemini report-title correction is bibliographic.

P1.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the narrative: methodology precedes results, discussion becomes separate Related Work, Conclusion, and Limitations sections, and the introduction is condensed. It also revises heading hierarchy, adopts author-year citations, and places references before the remaining appendix.

P2.justification: The document changes from one column to two, with extensive resizing, repositioning, and caption shortening. Table B2 becomes main-text Table 1, Figures C1 and E2 become Figures 5 and 8, and Tables D3 and F4 disappear. Existing diagrams and plots are reformatted without new main-result displays.

improvement.justification: v4 makes methods and supporting displays easier to locate, but removes the MCQ-order robustness evidence, detailed significance results, and important evaluation and implementation disclosures. These losses make the unchanged central findings harder to scrutinize and reproduce. The retained core evidence limits the deterioration, but the presentation benefits do not compensate for reduced transparency.
